claims.text: HfZrTiTa0.53 has quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa, compressive strength of 1314 MPa, and fracture strain of 13.5%.
The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a coarse initial microstructure.
The dynamic-recrystallization onset temperature of HfZrTiTa0.53 is approximately 300°C.
Preheating HfZrTiTa0.53 near 300°C and dynamically compressing it at about 10^4 s^-1 under adiabatic conditions will trigger in situ dynamic recrystallization.
Dynamic recrystallization can produce a refined, equiaxed grain structure.
The dynamically recrystallized grains will continuously refresh the microstructure during high-rate deformation.
Preheating reduces the critical energy barrier for dynamic recrystallization.
Fine dynamically recrystallized grains impede dislocation motion.
Fine dynamically recrystallized grains increase the work-hardening rate of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Fine dynamically recrystallized grains redistribute localized strain.
The proposed treatment will delay shear-band nucleation and reduce rapid failure.
The proposed treatment will modestly increase yield and compressive strengths relative to the baseline.
The proposed treatment will improve fracture strain by 15–25% relative to the baseline.
The increase in fracture strain represents improved uniform deformability.
The proposed treatment will increase impact-induced energy absorption through improved strain-rate hardening.
The predicted improvements apply under adiabatic dynamic compression at strain rates around 10^4 s^-1.
Accurate temperature control can activate dynamic recrystallization without causing undesirable static recrystallization or thermal damage.
The precise dynamic-recrystallization onset temperature for HfZrTiTa0.53 under high-rate loading is uncertain.

The matched experiment compares untreated and preheated HfZrTiTa0.53 specimens under the same dynamic-compression conditions and measures strength, fracture strain, shear-band onset, energy absorption, grain size, and dynamic recrystallization.

Failure to obtain at least a 15% fracture-strain improvement together with delayed shear-band initiation, or failure to observe fine equiaxed dynamically recrystallized grains, is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome is framed relative to a quasi-static baseline, whereas the matched experiment compares preheated and untreated specimens both under dynamic loading. These are different reference comparisons, so the experiment does not directly test every stated baseline-relative prediction.
